source.title: Parallel Training of Deep Networks with Local Updates
source.authors: M. Laskin; Luke Metz; Seth Nabarrao; Mark Saroufim; Badreddine Noune; C. Luschi; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; P. Abbeel

record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label memorization and natural-label training/test performance for backpropagation versus greedy local updates, a different method applied to the same capacity/generalization question.
record.gate_note: Figure 6(c) reports the study's own CIFAR-10 random-label training comparison. Figure 6(b) reports train/test accuracy by chunk size on natural labels. The broader throughput and optimization comparisons do not directly test the mapped claim versions.
record.test_reason: The ResNet18/CIFAR-10 experiments measure random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under global and local updates, bearing on V1 in a new architecture and training setting. The supplied text does not establish near-perfect random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that local parallelism offers speed and hardware-efficiency advantages in high-compute regimes, with performance tradeoffs. Larger chunks improve generalization, and global backpropagation memorizes random labels better than greedy local training. Roughly equal training loss across chunk sizes refers specifically to Figure 6(b).
record.recipe_differences: Uses local layer-wise updates and compares them with global backpropagation; the random-label experiment is a ResNet18 CIFAR-10 capacity comparison, not the source claim's model/recipe suite.
record.method_sensitivity: Training method (global backpropagation versus greedy local updates) changes random-label memorization capacity; chunk size changes natural-label generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller local training chunks worsen natural-label generalization despite similar training performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting backpropagation to smaller layer groups can increase the generalization gap in ResNet18 on CIFAR-10.

record.problems: Random-label evidence is presented only in a figure without exact values; the supplied text does not report random-label test accuracy. The natural-label chunk-size figure likewise supplies no exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other experiments compare compute cost, wall time, throughput, communication, and memory, which do not directly measure a listed claim version. Figure 7 feature visualizations are qualitative and do not measure the train/test gap. No additional qualifying rows identified.

untested.parts: Random-label held-out accuracy; the original architecture suite and ImageNet comparison; and a documented match of the natural-label and random-label training recipes without explicit regularization.
Held-out error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance separated by adaptive versus SGD optimizer under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out performance separated by batch size under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

missing.what: Intermediate chunk conditions in Figure 6(b): five, four, three and two layers have approximately 99% training accuracy and 91%, 91%, 90% and 89% test accuracy, respectively. These complete the natural-label comparison associated with V1.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is assigned because near-perfect random-label fitting cannot be established from the supplied curve transcription. Natural-label generalization alone does not establish coexistence with that capacity, and poorer greedy memorization alone does not establish a failure of V1. Batch-size and optimizer sweeps are pooled into performance frontiers rather than reported as the controlled comparisons required for V4 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with random labels under backpropagation and greedy local training, and reports train/test behavior in a separate natural-label chunk-size ablation. Does not test small Inception, AlexNet, MLPs, or ImageNet; random-label held-out accuracy is not reported.
